text:
maria: Quick checkin — after last night's runtime push we saw tail latency regressions for medium-long seq workloads (1k-4k). attaching the nightly flame/profile. perf-bot posted:

perf-bot: nightly-profile: prefill->decode handoff spike. top hotspot: kernel_matmul_fused_v2 @ prefill end (40% CPU), plus KV stall on first decode chunk.

aj: Did the kernel-selector roll out the new affinity patch to 8k/4k buckets? 

kevin: Yeah, rolled last night. Default affinity now biases fused kernels for batch sizes > 4. Observed 15% throughput uplift in microbench but maybe hurts mixed prefills.

dmitri: Can you paste the batch composition histogram + KV hit rates from the canary? Need to see full distribution.

maria: paste output:
```
batch_size_histogram: {1: 1200, 2: 980, 4: 430, 8: 210, 16: 80}
median_tokens_per_batch: 500
token_budget_target: 1024
kv_cache_hit_rate_prefill: 0.12
kv_cache_hit_rate_decode: 0.68
``` 

maria: Note: lots of small batches for short prompts, but the regression is at the tail for mixed long-prefill requests where prefill fires fused kernel then decode stalls waiting on KV.

aj: Hypothesis: fused kernel wins for pure matmul heavy prefill, but when mixed with decode's KV reads the handoff introduces synchronous stall. Suggest split queues: prefill-only queue that prioritizes kernel affinity and a decode queue with stricter token_budget per request.

kevin: Also saw a KV priming micro-regression — warmup not kicking in because prefill batches get fused kernel execution path which bypasses a small KV touch we rely on to populate L2. We can add an optional 'kv_touch' step for prefill when seq > 512.

maria: Proposed canary config:
```
routing:
  queueing:
    prefill_queue: true
    decode_queue: true
  batching:
    prefill_max_tokens: 2048
    decode_max_tokens: 256
    token_budget_prefill: 1500
    token_budget_decode: 300
kernel_selector:
  affinity_overrides:
    prefill: prefer_fused
    decode: prefer_standard
kv:
  priming: enable_for_prefill_seq_gt_512: true
```

perf-bot: canary-run results (12h): tail p99 latency down 18% on canary vs baseline, throughput neutral, kv_cache_hit_rate_prefill increased to 0.45, decode stall rate decreased 60%.

dmitri: Nice. Can we A/B for a day on live traffic for 10% of hosts? Keep tracing hooks to mark prefill vs decode queues.

maria: Scheduling the canary now. I'll push rollout config and link the dashboard. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

aj: If this stabilizes, follow-up: model-specific kernel profiles per family to avoid blanket fused bias.

kevin: Agreed. Also let's add a microbench that simulates prefill->decode handoff with KV priming to keep regression guarded.

maria: noted — I'll add eval & alert. Closing the loop after 24h canary.
